slides.texte_overlay:
how to become
easier to talk to
Smile with your eyes when someone approaches. A warm face before you even speak tells people they're welcome. Most people decide in a second if you're approachable.
Lose the headphones in social places. At the gym, the café, the office kitchen. Headphones say "don't talk to me," even when you'd love a conversation.
React with your face. Raise your eyebrows at a surprise, laugh at the funny part. Visible reactions show people you're enjoying the chat, and they open up more.
Don't correct small details. Wrong date, wrong name of a film, it doesn't matter. Letting small things go keeps the conversation flowing and people relaxed.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll always have something interesting to add, and people will love talking to you.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll always have something interesting to add.

slides.texte_overlay: Admit your own small fails. "I got lost three times on the way here." Little confessions make you human and help others feel comfortable sharing theirs.
Be the same with everyone. Friendly to the intern and the boss, the waiter and the client. People feel safe around someone who treats everyone with the same respect.
